figures.cap: triangle TVU with TV = 7.5 m, VU = 4.8 m, TU = 10.4 m

solutions.latex:
Using the cosine rule with the angle $\angle TVU$ opposite side $TU$:
$$\cos C = \dfrac{a^2 + b^2 - c^2}{2ab}$$
$$\begin{aligned} \cos \angle TVU &= \dfrac{4.8^2 + 7.5^2 - 10.4^2}{2 \times 4.8 \times 7.5} \\ &= -0.4009\ldots \\ \angle TVU &= 113^\circ 38' \end{aligned}$$
$$\therefore\ \angle TVU \approx 114^\circ \text{ (nearest degree)}$$
criteria: Substitutes correctly into the cosine rule, or equivalent merit

figures.cap: triangle XYZ with XY = 5 m, YZ = 1.5 m, angle at Y 40 degrees, XZ = x m

solutions.latex:
Using the cosine rule in the triangle with sides $1.5$ and $5$ and included angle $40^\circ$,
$$x^2 = 1.5^2 + 5^2 - 2\times 1.5\times 5\times\cos 40^\circ$$
$$\begin{aligned} x &= \sqrt{1.5^2 + 5^2 - 2\times 1.5\times 5\times\cos 40^\circ} \\ &= 3.969\ldots \\ &\approx 4.0 \text{ m} \end{aligned}$$
$$\therefore\ x \approx 4.0 \text{ m}$$
criteria: Correct cosine rule substitution (rounding ignored), or equivalent merit

parts.latex:
The largest angle in the triangle is $\theta^\circ$. What is the value of $\cos\theta^\circ$?

\exfigure{706_q5_1}

solutions.latex:
The largest angle is opposite the longest side, $7$. It lies between the sides $5$ and $6$.

Using the cosine rule, $c^2 = a^2 + b^2 - 2ab\cos C$, with $c = 7$, $a = 5$, $b = 6$,
$$7^2 = 5^2 + 6^2 - 2\times 5\times 6\cos\theta$$
$$\cos\theta = \dfrac{5^2 + 6^2 - 7^2}{2\times 5\times 6}$$

meta.self_check: Largest angle opposite largest side; cos is positive here (25+36-49=12), so angle acute, fine

Find the size of the $\angle BAC$ in triangle $ABC$, correct to the nearest degree.

\exfigure{706_q26_1}

solutions.latex:
Using the cosine rule in $\triangle ABC$:
$$\begin{aligned} \cos \angle BAC &= \dfrac{83^2 + 50^2 - 40^2}{2 \times 83 \times 50} \\ &= 0.9384337349\ldots \\ \angle BAC &= \cos^{-1}(0.9384337349\ldots) \\ &= 20.20983541\ldots^\circ \end{aligned}$$
$$\therefore\ \angle BAC = 20^\circ$$
